rationale: The workflow runs `npm ci` in both the lint and test jobs on every run, repeatedly fetching Node dependencies, and the repository pins a `package-lock.json` that can serve as a stable cache input. This matches the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE dependency-download caching pattern (evidence: experiment:batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9), which showed measured elapsed-time savings for caching dependency downloads keyed on a lockfile. I added an `actions/cache@v4` step for `~/.npm` before `npm ci` in both jobs, keyed on `hashFiles('package-lock.json')` with a restore-key fallback. All existing steps (checkout, setup-node, prettier check, expo type generation, typecheck, tests) are preserved unchanged, so build/test coverage is intact. No permissions, secrets, publishing/deployment, or new network access are introduced; the cache writes only to GitHub Actions' own cache service.
